# Roadmap, as a list

What Launchway does today and what is planned, in milestones marked Now, Next and Later. The same
items are drawn on the [roadmap](./public/roadmap.html), and each milestone has a detail page. As of 2026-11-21.

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/build-roadmap.mjs from docs/roadmap/roadmap.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Launchway is one place to host your code, build it, test it, scan it and deliver it, on servers you control or as a hosted service. It aims to be complete without being complicated: every task is a guided wizard, every capability is also in the API, the command line, the agent endpoint and Terraform, and the only things it needs are a database and Git. AI helps where you ask for it and stays off where you do not, and every run, change and approval is a durable record you can audit.

## Where Launchway stands today

**Already strong.**

- Delivery with verification and rollback: a deployment is checked, and you can return to the last good state even after it succeeded.
- Failures that explain themselves: a failed run says why, with the evidence, and re-runs from the failed step.
- Pipelines you can see: steps drawn the way they run, and a change followed from idea to running software.
- Runs on your own hardware: one program and a database, with no outside service required.
- Install, secrets and sign-in: a guided installer, secrets sealed under a key kept outside the database, and built-in accounts with a second factor.

**Not there yet.**

- The first self-upgrade exposed upgrade-ordering problems that are now fixed and guarded by tests, and the upgrade gate is still being finished.
- Most of the new work is built on separate branches and in final integration; it counts as Available only when it is on the main branch.
- The wall between Bases and sign-up, so people outside a team can use the hosted service: not built yet.
- Works alongside a hosted code host without moving repositories: planned.
- Windows and macOS runners, and the mobile and games needs that follow them.
- Maturity: Launchway is young, has few users and has not been through an independent security audit or a certification.

Much of what is listed as in progress is built and tested but not yet merged; it counts as Available only when it is.


## Who Launchway is for

These four come first. After them the aim is a product that larger companies would also choose to use.

- **Self-hosting.** One small machine runs everything, stable and low cost, with nothing leaving the house. Delivery, backup and restore you can trust. *A good fit now; the guided installer is on the main branch.*
- **The small team.** Zero setup, free to start, real deployments later, and no need to move code that already lives on a hosted code host. *Not yet: working alongside a hosted code host and sign-up are planned.*
- **The freelancer.** A laptop and many clients: demos fast, sites that look and rank well, cheap hosting, and a clean hand-over to each client. *Weak today: previews, a space per client and site starters are planned.*
- **Mobile and games.** Apple and Windows build machines, signing and store upload, very large files and long builds. *Not yet: the build machines come first.*


## The order we are building in

After what is already in flight, in this order.

1. **The wall between Bases, then sign-up.** Several Bases on one installation, isolated and proven by tests, then sign-up with the least setup. ([area page](roadmap/hosted-service.md))
2. **Merge and deploy the finished rounds.** What is built is joined, tested together, and put to use. ([area page](roadmap/build-order.md))
3. **The upgrade gate and network detection.** Upgrades that cannot half-apply, chart values that stay compatible, and detection of network problems before they bite. ([area page](roadmap/installing.md))
4. **Works alongside a hosted code host.** Connect repositories without moving them, run pipelines on your own machines and report back to the pull request there. ([area page](roadmap/git-hosting.md))
5. **Rollout drill-down and control.** See and control every object a delivery created. ([area page](roadmap/delivery.md))
6. **Delivery by choice.** GitOps controller, direct chart installs or plain manifests, and previews for every pull request. ([area page](roadmap/delivery.md))
7. **The Depot as one area.** Everything stored in one place, with scans and a proxy cache. ([area page](roadmap/registry.md))
8. **Editor plug-ins and one-step setup for agent tools.** Launchway where developers already work. ([area page](roadmap/developer-experience.md))
9. **Agents that deliver, natively.** A sandboxed agent machine and the model gateway. ([area page](roadmap/ai.md))
10. **Windows and macOS runners.** A first basic version, then signing and store upload. ([area page](roadmap/pipelines.md))


**What changed in the roadmap, 21 November 2026.**

- Every request from today is now in the roadmap, in the milestone where it belongs, with an honest status.
- Work and agents: work tracking, release management, agents that deliver (with levels of autonomy, independent review and spending limits), and keeping services healthy by detecting, diagnosing and, where policy allows, fixing.
- Your editor and your own systems: editor plug-ins, one-step setup for agent tools, an optional development environment in the browser, and extension points so site-specific systems never live in the product.
- Organized and personal: folders and search on every list, shared and personal layouts, a home page based on what needs attention, home panels, an address for every view, and live streaming with time estimates.
- The Depot (one area for everything stored), delivery by choice (GitOps controller, direct chart installs or plain manifests), drill-down from a deploy into every object it created, every cloud and on-premises within the environment's limits, one graph from code to hardware, and adopting machines that already exist.
- A new short section, Who Launchway is for, and the build order now follows the order decided today.
- Statuses checked against the main branch: the guided installer, built-in accounts with a second factor, encryption at rest, fair queueing, path filters, restricted pull requests, notifications, dependency updates, offline validation and the delivery fixes are now Available. Everything built on a separate branch is In progress, marked as built and in final integration.
- Duplicate rows for the same work were merged.


Order is by value, not a schedule, and plans change. An item is **available** only when it is on the
main branch, tested and documented. Launchway is not certified against any compliance standard;
compliance items provide controls and evidence.

## Available today

| Item | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| Pipelines as code | Typed YAML with steps, dependencies, run inputs, outputs passed between steps and loops, kept in Git next to the code they build. ([more](guide/pipelines.md)) |
| Flow control | Conditions on steps, retries with back-off, lanes that make runs take turns, run timeouts, and re-running from any step with what each step was given. ([more](reference/pipeline.md#when)) |
| Build caches | Dependencies kept between runs in the database, with entries a pull request can write but the default branch never reads. ([more](guide/build-caches.md)) |
| Triggers | Push, pull request (with target-branch filters, and newer pushes cancelling older runs), manual, schedule and webhook. ([more](guide/triggers.md)) |
| Shared libraries | Templates and scripts in their own repository, pinned by tag, branch or commit, with typed parameters. ([more](guide/libraries.md)) |
| Step resources | Each step is sized, with defaults per kind of step and a ceiling no step can pass, so one step cannot starve a cluster. ([more](reference/config-objects.md#step-resources)) |
| Configuration in the database | Projects, runner pools, environments, policies, models and more are objects in the database with history, audit and safe concurrent edits, never a file to hand-edit. ([more](guide/configuration.md)) |
| Four levels | Base, Wing, Squadron and Project (or the plain Installation, Organization, Team and Project), with words you choose and levels nobody uses kept out of sight. ([more](guide/configuration.md#levels)) |
| Guided setup wizards | First-run setup, connecting a repository, adding a runner, an environment, a policy or a verification step: plain questions, explained options, answers checked as you go. ([more](howto/setup-first-run.md)) |
| A guided interface | A Home page that says what to do next with a setup checklist, navigation whose sections and tabs appear only when there is something to show, and a run page that says why each wait is happening. ([more](demo.md)) |
| One capability, every interface | What the web UI does, the HTTP API, the command line and the agent endpoint do too, with a table in the build that fails when one falls behind. ([more](reference/interface-parity.md)) |
| High availability | Several servers on one PostgreSQL database with no leader; a run survives a server or a runner dying. SQLite for a single server. ([more](guide/high-availability.md)) |
| Quality gates | Lint, size, architecture, test and originality checks fail the build, so the code stays easy to change. ([more](development/quality-gates.md)) |
| GitOps with Argo CD | Deploy by Git commit, watch sync and health, control Argo Rollouts (promote, abort, retry), roll back, lock environments. ([more](guide/deployments.md)) |
| Applications view | The Argo CD applications a deploy runner has seen, shown with their status next to your environments. ([more](guide/deployments.md)) |
| Verification after a deploy | Checks on Prometheus, Loki, ClickHouse and OpenSearch with automatic abort or rollback; an optional model explains the verdict and never turns a failure into a pass. ([more](guide/verification.md)) |
| Container images | Rootless builds, scans, signatures, provenance and SBOMs, pushed to any OCI registry. ([more](guide/images.md)) |
| Approvals and protected environments | Approval steps; the person who started a run cannot approve its production deploy. ([more](guide/approvals-and-reruns.md)) |
| Policy gates | Rules pipelines cannot opt out of, at run start, before deploys and image pushes; report or enforce; audited, expiring waivers. ([more](guide/policies.md)) |
| Sign-in and access | OpenID Connect sign-in with groups, roles per project and environment, scoped API tokens and an audit trail. ([more](guide/access.md)) |
| Secrets that stay with runners | Pipelines hold references; runners read values from Vault, OpenBao, files or the environment, and mask them. ([more](guide/secrets.md)) |
| Security findings and SBOMs | Secret, code, dependency, license and image findings (SARIF), new and fixed across runs, and a component search. ([more](guide/security-findings.md)) |
| Secure step execution | Non-root step pods under strict pod security, a step pod removed when its run ends and leaked ones reaped, container and host executors, and runners that only connect outward. ([more](security/trust-model.md)) |
| Runner identity and pools | Join tokens, a key per runner, pools scoped to projects, and allow-lists on the runner itself. ([more](guide/runner-identity.md)) |
| Test, coverage and HTML reports | Thirteen test formats, coverage with thresholds, flaky-test detection, history, and the tools' own HTML reports in a sandbox. ([more](guide/test-reports.md)) |
| Built-in artifact storage | Artifacts and hosted reports live in the database by default, so several servers need nothing else; S3 or a shared folder are optional. ([more](artifacts.md)) |
| AI models in steps | Optional hosted or local models for steps and failure explanations, with per-model token limits; keys never enter a step's container. ([more](guide/ai.md)) |
| An endpoint for agents | Agents validate pipelines, start and watch runs and diagnose failures with exactly the rights of the token they hold. ([more](guide/agents.md)) |
| Open source | Free software under the AGPL-3.0, with a commercial license for those who cannot use it, and this documentation site with its roadmap. ([more](https://github.com/JK-Magic-Creations/launchway/blob/main/LICENSING.md)) |
| A public documentation site and roadmap | Enterprise-level documentation with diagrams, security guidance, a graphical roadmap with drill-down pages, and a local demo. ([more](start/overview.md)) |
| Launchway’s own words | Two built-in sets of words (aviation-flavored and plain business names), a rename for any word, and the same words in the interface, documentation and messages. ([more](guide/words.md)) |
| Learn, inside the product | The documentation of the release you are running, with pictures and an offline search, opened from the interface with no separate website. ([more](learn/start-here.md)) |
| Variables at levels | The same variable declared at a nearer level overrides the one above, with locks from above and a hierarchy view that shows where each value comes from. ([more](guide/variables.md)) |
| Shared pipeline templates and Flight plans | A template or a Flight plan set once for a Wing or Squadron, used by every project beneath it, with deploy, verify and approval steps included. ([more](guide/libraries.md)) |
| Rides through outages | Database errors are retried, runner writes are safe to repeat, a runner keeps its logs and results while the server is away, and a doctor command checks the database. ([more](guide/high-availability.md)) |
| Accessible by design | Automated scans, contrast tests and keyboard journeys run on every change, with a published conformance statement and a quality bar for the API, the agent endpoint and the command line. ([more](guide/accessibility.md)) |
| A failed step says why | Every failed step states its reason and cause with the evidence, can be re-run from that step, and the actions offered are only those that can work. ([more](guide/approvals-and-reruns.md)) |
| A push starts a run | A push to a hosted repository starts the matching pipeline, with markers to skip a run, and a minimum Git version checked at install. ([more](guide/triggers.md)) |
| Security scans as gates | Vulnerability, secret, dependency, image, chart and manifest scanning, fuzzing, an SBOM and security headers run on every change, backed by a security policy and a threat model. ([more](security/how-launchway-is-scanned.md)) |
| Pull requests and code review | Open, review, comment on lines, suggest changes and merge inside Launchway, with merge rules that block until required checks pass. ([more](guide/pull-requests.md)) |
| Pipelines drawn the way they run | Steps that run together appear side by side on the run page, drawn from their dependencies. |
| Rollback after a successful deployment | Return to the last stable state even after a rollout has succeeded, with the consequence shown first and a Logbook entry. ([more](guide/rollback-after-success.md)) |
| Queues, limits and path filters | Steps wait for room instead of failing, runs are limited and ordered fairly, documentation-only pushes skip the heavy steps, and untrusted pull requests run restricted. ([more](guide/queues.md)) |
| A guided installer | `launchway install` asks plain questions, shows what it will do, and sets up a laptop, a server or a Kubernetes cluster; a first-run guide follows in the browser. ([more](howto/install-in-ten-minutes.md)) |
| Built-in accounts with a second factor | Sign-in with passwords and authenticator codes, recovery codes, invitations and a one-time setup code; passkeys are not built yet. ([more](guide/built-in-accounts.md)) |
| Encryption at rest | Stored secrets are sealed under a root key kept outside the database; the key is created once, and a recovery command exists for a damaged key file. ([more](guide/encryption-at-rest.md)) |
| GitOps write-back and a built-in health proof | A deployment writes the new image into Git safely and checks the health of what it deployed without extra tools. ([more](guide/gitops-write-back.md)) |
| Notifications | Rules send run and delivery events to signed webhooks and chat channels, with a delivery log and retries. ([more](guide/notifications.md)) |
| Dependency update pull requests | Launchway proposes dependency updates as pull requests, with lock files regenerated in a container. ([more](guide/dependency-updates.md)) |
| Validate offline | `launchway validate` checks a pipeline without a server and can show the fully resolved result. ([more](reference/cli.md)) |
| Full import and a read-only issue archive | Import every ref of an existing repository and keep another server's issues as a read-only archive. ([more](reference/cli.md)) |
| Plain messages when a step is killed | A step killed for memory says so, with the limit and the setting to raise. ([more](guide/pipelines.md)) |

## Milestone 1: Host your code and run your pipelines in one place (Now)

A team can keep its repositories in Launchway, review and merge there, and run every pipeline it has, with everything a hosted CI service offers and nothing else to install. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-1.md).

| [Per-step runner and workspace](roadmap/milestone-1.md#per-step-runner-and-workspace) | Planned | Each step can choose its own image, runner and working area. |
| [Parallel steps drawn as parallel](roadmap/milestone-1.md#parallel-steps-drawn-as-parallel) | Available | Steps that run together are drawn side by side on the run page, so the shape of a pipeline is the shape you see. |
| [A step's user has an account entry](roadmap/milestone-1.md#a-step-s-user-has-an-account-entry) | Available | The user a step runs as is known to the system inside the step, so tools that look up a user, such as secure shell, work. |
| [Steps wait for room instead of failing](roadmap/milestone-1.md#steps-wait-for-room-instead-of-failing) | Available | A full step namespace makes a step wait, with the reason, the runs that hold the room and its place in line, instead of failing the build. ([docs](guide/queues.md)) |
| [Limits and a fair order for runs](roadmap/milestone-1.md#limits-and-a-fair-order-for-runs) | Available | Runs over a limit are held with a reason, in a visible order, and the main build is never held. ([docs](guide/queues.md)) |
| [Path filters on triggers and steps](roadmap/milestone-1.md#path-filters-on-triggers-and-steps) | Available | A documentation-only change builds the docs and skips the image and the deploy approvals. ([docs](reference/pipeline.md#path-filters)) |
| [Restricted runs for untrusted pull requests](roadmap/milestone-1.md#restricted-runs-for-untrusted-pull-requests) | Available | Pull requests from automation accounts and forks run without secrets, deploys or write caches until a maintainer approves. ([docs](guide/pull-request-trust.md)) |

| [One command, three targets](roadmap/milestone-1.md#one-command-three-targets) | Available | launchway install asks the same few plain questions for a laptop, a single server or Kubernetes, and ends by printing the address and the one-time step. |

| [A security checklist at the end](roadmap/milestone-1.md#a-security-checklist-at-the-end) | Available | The installer finishes with a plain checklist of what is protected and what to do next, and the doctor repeats it later. |

| [Every cluster feature checked](roadmap/milestone-1.md#every-cluster-feature-checked) | Planned | On an existing cluster the installer checks storage, a way in, certificates, a name, policy enforcement and rights, and offers a fix or a labeled trial option for each one missing. |
| [An offline bundle](roadmap/milestone-1.md#an-offline-bundle) | Planned | One file with everything Launchway needs, for networks with no internet. |

## Milestone 2: Deeper pipeline power, and a way off self-hosted automation servers (Next)

Pipelines can be as dynamic as real code needs, and a team running an automation server can move its jobs without losing what it relies on. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-2.md).

### Write pipelines your way

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Custom steps in your own language](roadmap/milestone-2.md#custom-steps-in-your-own-language) | Planned | A step is a program in your repository with typed inputs, outputs and secrets, runnable and testable on its own, so pipeline logic is ordinary tested code. |
| [A step contract and starter kits](roadmap/milestone-2.md#a-step-contract-and-starter-kits) | Planned | A published contract for what a step receives and returns, with starter kits for common languages. |
| [Steps run in a sandbox](roadmap/milestone-2.md#steps-run-in-a-sandbox) | Planned | Custom steps run in an isolated container with only the secrets and network they declared. |
| [Share and pin steps and templates](roadmap/milestone-2.md#share-and-pin-steps-and-templates) | Planned | Publish a custom step, not only a template, from a repository and pin users to a tag, branch or commit. Pinning templates this way already works. |
| [Generated pipelines](roadmap/milestone-2.md#generated-pipelines) | Planned | A step can print more steps in any language; Launchway checks them against the same schema and policy and shows them on the run. |
| [Expressions for conditions](roadmap/milestone-2.md#expressions-for-conditions) | Planned | A small typed expression language with no loops and no side effects, checked before the run; today's conditions keep working. ([docs](reference/pipeline.md#when)) |
| [Typed outputs between steps](roadmap/milestone-2.md#typed-outputs-between-steps) | Planned | A step declares what it passes on, and a reference to an output that does not exist fails before the run, not in the middle of it. |
| [A browsable catalog of templates and steps](roadmap/milestone-2.md#a-browsable-catalog-of-templates-and-steps) | Planned | Shared libraries pinned by tag already work; the catalog lets you find, compare and update them from inside the product. ([docs](guide/libraries.md)) |
| [Update notices for shared libraries](roadmap/milestone-2.md#update-notices-for-shared-libraries) | Planned | See which projects use an old version of a template and open an update as a reviewable change. |
| [A triggers page](roadmap/milestone-2.md#a-triggers-page) | Planned | One page showing every trigger and exactly which pipelines it starts. |
| [Event sources from queues and buses](roadmap/milestone-2.md#event-sources-from-queues-and-buses) | Planned | Start pipelines from message queues and event buses, with filters, and replies back. |
| [Steps as a graph of containers](roadmap/milestone-2.md#steps-as-a-graph-of-containers) | Planned | Lay steps out as a graph of containers with fan-out and join, for work that is not a straight line. |
| [Runners that keep themselves updated](roadmap/milestone-2.md#runners-that-keep-themselves-updated) | Planned | Runners on VMs and on customers' machines update under your policy, so the fleet never drifts. |
| [Pipeline history and flaky tests](roadmap/milestone-2.md#pipeline-history-and-flaky-tests) | Planned | Duration charts, pass rate and the slowest steps across runs, and flaky tests flagged on the pull request. Flaky detection and test history already work on the run page. |
| [Step pages](roadmap/milestone-2.md#step-pages) | Planned | Each step has a page: where its code lives, its inputs and types, and which pipelines use it. |
| [An event log that explains every decision](roadmap/milestone-2.md#an-event-log-that-explains-every-decision) | In progress | Every received event is listed with the decision for each trigger and why, can be replayed, and may come from a signed per-project webhook source with filters, deduplication and debouncing; a trigger can follow another project's result. |
| [Standing orders for every repository](roadmap/milestone-2.md#standing-orders-for-every-repository) | In progress | A profile of checks per language and ecosystem, set by level and kept in Git, with findings in one list; a gate that blocks only what a change introduces. |

| [Runners on personal machines hold back when busy](roadmap/milestone-2.md#runners-on-personal-machines-hold-back-when-busy) | Planned | A runner on a laptop or workstation stops taking work while the machine is busy, and respects the limits its owner sets. |

| [First signal fast](roadmap/milestone-2.md#first-signal-fast) | Planned | A time budget for the first result on a pull request, with fast checks first and deep checks later. |
| [A first green build in ten minutes](roadmap/milestone-2.md#a-first-green-build-in-ten-minutes) | Planned | Detect the tool, apply the recipe and its Flight plan, and get a green build, with the clock as a test. |

| [Builds on macOS and Windows machines](roadmap/milestone-2.md#builds-on-macos-and-windows-machines) | Planned | Runners for Apple and Windows, signing and store upload, very large files and long builds, for mobile and games. |
| [A development environment in the browser, optional](roadmap/milestone-2.md#a-development-environment-in-the-browser-optional) | Planned | Use a full editor environment inside Launchway, turned on by choice and off by default; it is made available, not copied. |

## Milestone 3: Delivery and GitOps depth (Next)

See and control everything you run, whether it is an application in a cluster, a virtual machine or an image-based host, and deliver to it safely. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-3.md).

| [A health proof built into verification](roadmap/milestone-3.md#a-health-proof-built-into-verification) | Available | A verify step can call the service it just deployed, over its window, with no monitoring series to set up; a failure says how many requests got which answer. ([docs](guide/verification.md)) |

([docs](guide/gitops-write-back.md)) |

([docs](guide/libraries.md)) |

Images, Helm charts and other OCI artifacts stored beside the code, under the same permissions and policies. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-4.md).

| [More package formats](roadmap/milestone-4.md#more-package-formats) | Planned | Language and system packages, such as for common programming languages, with cleanup rules and quotas. |
| [Any other registry, equally](roadmap/milestone-4.md#any-other-registry-equally) | Available | Pushing to any OCI registry works today and stays first class beside the built-in one. ([docs](guide/images.md)) |
| [Pipelines that build, test and publish only](roadmap/milestone-4.md#pipelines-that-build-test-and-publish-only) | Planned | Not everything deploys: a pipeline for a library, command-line tool, image or chart ends at published and available. |
| [Native endpoints for package clients](roadmap/milestone-4.md#native-endpoints-for-package-clients) | Planned | Go and npm clients talk to Launchway directly, and Python, Maven, NuGet, Cargo and RubyGems follow. |
| [Who uses which version](roadmap/milestone-4.md#who-uses-which-version) | Planned | A library page shows which projects fetched which version and which are behind. |
| [The Depot: one area for everything stored](roadmap/milestone-4.md#the-depot-one-area-for-everything-stored) | In progress | Container images, charts, packages, operating-system and machine images, build caches, state and files are browsed in one searchable place with folders, vulnerabilities, signatures, a proxy cache, replication and policies. |

## Milestone 5: The software graph, with automated patching (Later)

One connected picture of code, dependencies, images and deployments, so you always know what runs where and can fix it safely. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-5.md).

### Know what you run

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Findings and SBOMs per run](roadmap/milestone-5.md#findings-and-sboms-per-run) | Available | The starting point already works: findings and components recorded for every run. ([docs](guide/security-findings.md)) |
| [What is deployed where](roadmap/milestone-5.md#what-is-deployed-where) | Planned | Link every deployed image back to its commit, its components and its findings, including on hosts Launchway only observes. |
| [A continuous observer of what runs](roadmap/milestone-5.md#a-continuous-observer-of-what-runs) | Planned | Watch clusters and hosts for what is actually running, not only what was deployed. |
| [Continuous scanning of what runs](roadmap/milestone-5.md#continuous-scanning-of-what-runs) | Planned | Scan deployed software for new vulnerabilities and best-practice gaps, not only at build time. |
| [Advisories, exceptions and licenses](roadmap/milestone-5.md#advisories-exceptions-and-licenses) | Planned | Record which vulnerabilities apply, import vendor statements that they do not, and check licenses. |
| [Who owns what](roadmap/milestone-5.md#who-owns-what) | Planned | Each component, service and repository has an owner, and findings go to that owner. |
| [Code search across repositories](roadmap/milestone-5.md#code-search-across-repositories) | Planned | Search symbols and text across every repository, hosted or connected, filtered by what you may see. |
| [Code intelligence](roadmap/milestone-5.md#code-intelligence) | Planned | Definitions, references and call information, for people and for agents. |
| [Code knowledge for AI, with fewer tokens](roadmap/milestone-5.md#code-knowledge-for-ai-with-fewer-tokens) | Planned | Answer AI questions from a graph of code and deployments instead of pasting files. |
| [Blast radius of a vulnerability](roadmap/milestone-5.md#blast-radius-of-a-vulnerability) | Planned | From an advisory, see which deployed services and environments are affected and who owns them. |
| [One graph from code to hardware](roadmap/milestone-5.md#one-graph-from-code-to-hardware) | In progress | The software graph holds code and what it needs, what is built from it (images per architecture, operating-system images, machine images), the machines that satisfy those needs, and what is deployed where, with the source of every link. |

### Fix it safely

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Automated patching](roadmap/milestone-5.md#automated-patching) | Planned | Off by default and turned on per zone: updates open as changes, pass tests and change management, and roll out through Argo CD. |
| [Built-in dependency updates](roadmap/milestone-5.md#built-in-dependency-updates) | Available | Launchway finds outdated and vulnerable dependencies in a repository and proposes the updates as ordinary reviewable pull requests, so no outside update robot is needed. |
| [Lock files regenerated in a container and checked](roadmap/milestone-5.md#lock-files-regenerated-in-a-container-and-checked) | In progress | When an update changes a dependency, the lock file is rebuilt in an isolated container and the result is verified before the pull request is opened. |
| [Image refresh and patching of base images](roadmap/milestone-5.md#image-refresh-and-patching-of-base-images) | Planned | Rebuild images when their base changes and roll the new ones out. |
| [AI-proposed fixes](roadmap/milestone-5.md#ai-proposed-fixes) | Planned | An optional helper proposes a fix or an upgrade note, flagged as AI, never merged on its own. |
| [Patch deadlines and evidence](roadmap/milestone-5.md#patch-deadlines-and-evidence) | Planned | Track how long each vulnerability has been open and produce evidence of patching within your own deadline. |

### Build and release in dependency order

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [One dependency graph, with where each link came from](roadmap/milestone-5.md#one-dependency-graph-with-where-each-link-came-from) | Planned | Every link says where it was found, how sure Launchway is and offers the fix right there: add a link, ignore a wrong one with a reason. |
| [Libraries first, then what uses them](roadmap/milestone-5.md#libraries-first-then-what-uses-them) | Planned | When a library changes it is built and published first, and each application that uses it is built after, once, in order. |
| [Dependents checked before a change merges](roadmap/milestone-5.md#dependents-checked-before-a-change-merges) | Planned | A library’s pull request builds the applications that use it against the new version and reports the result. |
| [Limits on build storms](roadmap/milestone-5.md#limits-on-build-storms) | Planned | Batching and caps keep one library change from starting a flood of dependent builds. |
| [Order you can override](roadmap/milestone-5.md#order-you-can-override) | Planned | Set build and release order by hand, pin a version, and mark an edge wrong; the system works out the order and a person can always override. |
| [Formations: things that go together](roadmap/milestone-5.md#formations-things-that-go-together) | Planned | A Formation is a release unit of applications, databases and configuration that are delivered together in the right order. |
| [One go or no-go, one watch, one way back](roadmap/milestone-5.md#one-go-or-no-go-one-watch-one-way-back) | Planned | A Formation has one decision, one timeline and one watch, and returns to the stable state in reverse order. |
| [Database first, then the application](roadmap/milestone-5.md#database-first-then-the-application) | Planned | A Formation expands the database first, deploys services in dependency order and finishes the contract step later. |
| [Linked changes across repositories](roadmap/milestone-5.md#linked-changes-across-repositories) | Planned | One change that spans several repositories is tracked, tested and merged together. |
| [Branching patterns as Flight plans](roadmap/milestone-5.md#branching-patterns-as-flight-plans) | Planned | Trunk-based, short-lived branches with pull requests, the long-lived develop-and-release flow, release branches, tag-based library releases, forks, pull-request promotion and monorepos each come as a Flight plan. |
| [A recommender for the branching pattern](roadmap/milestone-5.md#a-recommender-for-the-branching-pattern) | Planned | When a repository is created or imported, six plain questions lead to the simplest pattern that fits, with the reason and the trade-offs, set up in one step. |

## Milestone 6: AI as an optional first-class helper (Next)

AI wherever it saves effort, always optional, always off until an administrator turns a purpose on, and never able to hide a failure. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-6.md).

### Today

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Models in steps and verification](roadmap/milestone-6.md#models-in-steps-and-verification) | Available | Hosted or local models in steps, with explanations of failures and verdicts that never override a failing check. ([docs](guide/ai.md)) |
| [Agents as users](roadmap/milestone-6.md#agents-as-users) | Available | The agent endpoint gives agents the same permissions, limits and audit as any user. ([docs](guide/agents.md)) |

### A gateway of your own

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [A built-in model gateway](roadmap/milestone-6.md#a-built-in-model-gateway) | Planned | One endpoint that routes to any hosted or self-hosted model, with usage monitoring and easy switching of providers. |
| [Local and self-hosted models](roadmap/milestone-6.md#local-and-self-hosted-models) | Planned | Run and serve open models on your own machines and use them like any other. |
| [Provider switching and fallbacks](roadmap/milestone-6.md#provider-switching-and-fallbacks) | Planned | Change provider or model in one place, with fallbacks if one is down. |
| [Usage monitoring](roadmap/milestone-6.md#usage-monitoring) | Planned | See usage by model, project and purpose, with cost. |
| [Spending limits](roadmap/milestone-6.md#spending-limits) | Planned | Budgets in money, per model, project and purpose, not only in tokens. |
| [AI off until a purpose is turned on](roadmap/milestone-6.md#ai-off-until-a-purpose-is-turned-on) | Planned | Every purpose, such as explaining failures or reviewing changes, is off until an administrator turns it on. |
| [Context compression](roadmap/milestone-6.md#context-compression) | Planned | Shrink what is sent to a model without losing file paths, line numbers or error codes, with every omission marked and the saving measured. |
| [A protected path for regulated data](roadmap/milestone-6.md#a-protected-path-for-regulated-data) | Planned | Use only models whose data-handling terms you have recorded, so that regulated projects never reach the wrong one. |
| [Models that know Launchway](roadmap/milestone-6.md#models-that-know-launchway) | Planned | Optional models tuned on Launchway itself, runnable locally and never trained on customer data. |
| [From a picture to a pipeline](roadmap/milestone-6.md#from-a-picture-to-a-pipeline) | Planned | Design a delivery visually and have AI help translate it into a pipeline you can read and edit. |
| [AI summaries and review of changes](roadmap/milestone-6.md#ai-summaries-and-review-of-changes) | Planned | Optional summaries and review comments on pull requests, labelled as AI. |
| [AI help with failures](roadmap/milestone-6.md#ai-help-with-failures) | Planned | Explain why a deploy failed as well as a step, with the evidence used. Explaining a failed step already works. |
| [Agent guidance and an agent catalog](roadmap/milestone-6.md#agent-guidance-and-an-agent-catalog) | Planned | Ready-made instructions so agents know how to use Launchway, and a list of agents with their permissions. |

### Agents that deliver

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Assign a story to an agent](roadmap/milestone-6.md#assign-a-story-to-an-agent) | Planned | An agent runs on a sandboxed machine of your own, works from a story, and opens a pull request under the same rules as a person; no secrets, a budget, and a kill switch from the start. |
| [Autonomy levels set by policy](roadmap/milestone-6.md#autonomy-levels-set-by-policy) | Planned | Choose how much an agent may do, per environment, from suggesting to delivering; production stays at a low level until a person raises it with a written reason. |
| [An independent reviewing agent](roadmap/milestone-6.md#an-independent-reviewing-agent) | Planned | Where policy allows, a separate session with a different identity and no shared context may approve listed kinds of change, with a share of changes sampled by people. |
| [Spend wisely](roadmap/milestone-6.md#spend-wisely) | Planned | Route each task to the right model for its difficulty, use plain tools before any model, keep a share of capacity in reserve for interactive work, and show spend against limits. |
| [One interface for developers, designers and owners](roadmap/milestone-6.md#one-interface-for-developers-designers-and-owners) | Planned | Assign, review and watch agent work, spend and results in one place, with the same permissions and audit trail as everything else. |

## Milestone 7: The hosted service, the public demo and enterprise controls (Next)

Sign up and go, or keep your files on your own machines; hosted, hosted with your own machines, or self-hosted, with easy moves between them, and a wall around every customer’s Base. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-7.md).

### Hosted service and demo

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Hosted service](roadmap/milestone-7.md#hosted-service) | Planned | Launchway as a service: sign-up, quotas, usage metering, a free plan with every feature on, pay for use, and data residency. |
| [Free tier and pay for use](roadmap/milestone-7.md#free-tier-and-pay-for-use) | Planned | A free tier, and pay-for-use billing from the start, with no extras for basics. |
| [Data residency](roadmap/milestone-7.md#data-residency) | Planned | Choose where your data lives. |
| [Runners on your machines](roadmap/milestone-7.md#runners-on-your-machines) | Planned | Runners on your own servers or clusters connect out to the hosted engine, so code and secrets never leave your network. |
| [Sandboxed hosted runners](roadmap/milestone-7.md#sandboxed-hosted-runners) | Planned | Each step in its own isolated machine, with no route to anything but the internet and firm quotas; the same profile available to any self-hosted server. |
| [Hosted capacity that can grow](roadmap/milestone-7.md#hosted-capacity-that-can-grow) | Planned | Everything is portable, so capacity can be added on any provider as demand justifies. |
| [A public demo](roadmap/milestone-7.md#a-public-demo) | Planned | A safe instance on the internet with realistic data anyone can explore, read-only at first. A local demo already runs from the quick start. ([docs](demo.md)) |
| [Several Wings on one Base](roadmap/milestone-7.md#several-wings-on-one-base) | Planned | Several Wings on one installation, isolated from each other, with the level names you choose. |

### Sign up and go

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Sign up with the least set-up](roadmap/milestone-7.md#sign-up-with-the-least-set-up) | Planned | One front door where anyone signs up with an email address or an existing account, proves the address, protects the account, names their Base and lands in a guided first project. |
| [Passkeys, authenticator apps and recovery codes](roadmap/milestone-7.md#passkeys-authenticator-apps-and-recovery-codes) | Planned | The account is bound to something only its owner has: a passkey, preferably, or an authenticator app, with recovery codes shown once. The owner and every administrator must use one of the strong ones. |
| [Recovery that is not a back door](roadmap/milestone-7.md#recovery-that-is-not-a-back-door) | Planned | A lost second factor is recovered through the other factors you set up, or through a waiting period with notices to every session and to the account’s email. |
| [Sign-up protection that respects privacy](roadmap/milestone-7.md#sign-up-protection-that-respects-privacy) | Planned | Rate limits, a small puzzle the browser solves and friction for throwaway addresses guard the form, with no tracking, no outside challenge service and no phone numbers. |
| [A guided first project](roadmap/milestone-7.md#a-guided-first-project) | Planned | Pick a starter, create or import a repository, push or edit in the browser, see a green build, and invite a teammate with one link. |
| [Protected both ways](roadmap/milestone-7.md#protected-both-ways) | Planned | The service is protected from its customers’ code and content, and customers are protected from the operator and from each other. |
| [Leave completely](roadmap/milestone-7.md#leave-completely) | Planned | Export a whole Base in an open format, then delete it: after a grace period its keys are destroyed, which makes every copy, including backups, unreadable, and a certificate says so. |
| [Addresses on one domain](roadmap/milestone-7.md#addresses-on-one-domain) | Planned | Each Base is a first-level name under one domain, with one wildcard record and one certificate, so nobody buys a second domain and DNS stays simple. |

### Three ways to run, and easy moves between them

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Fully hosted](roadmap/milestone-7.md#fully-hosted) | Planned | The default: repositories, pipelines, runners, secrets, registry and reports all on the hosted service, with nothing to install. |
| [Hosted with your own Detachment](roadmap/milestone-7.md#hosted-with-your-own-detachment) | Planned | The hosted screens and coordination, with builds, secrets and deployments on your side. |
| [Files on your own machines, through a sealed relay](roadmap/milestone-7.md#files-on-your-own-machines-through-a-sealed-relay) | Planned | Two people, two houses, no hosted copies: each runs one command, and both reach the files through Launchway over an end-to-end encrypted session that the relay carries but cannot read. |
| [Replicas across two machines](roadmap/milestone-7.md#replicas-across-two-machines) | Planned | With two machines, every repository has a full copy on each, pushes go to whichever is reachable, and they catch up with each other when both are online. |
| [Backup and recovery on your own machines](roadmap/milestone-7.md#backup-and-recovery-on-your-own-machines) | Planned | The second machine is a live copy, and an optional encrypted backup goes to storage you own, with a walk-through for “my laptop died”. |
| [Self-hosted, the same product](roadmap/milestone-7.md#self-hosted-the-same-product) | Planned | Everything on your own machines, installed with the guided installer, with the same features and the same export format. |
| [Guided moves between the three](roadmap/milestone-7.md#guided-moves-between-the-three) | Planned | Move one project or a whole Base, in either direction, from a button or one command, after a preview that lists what will move and what you must decide. |
| [Secrets move without being exposed](roadmap/milestone-7.md#secrets-move-without-being-exposed) | Planned | Secret values are re-sealed to the destination’s key, exported under a passphrase only you know, or re-entered and rotated, so they are never in the clear on the way. |

### A size ceiling, with notices, and nothing held hostage

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Size ceilings on hosted Bases](roadmap/milestone-7.md#size-ceilings-on-hosted-bases) | Planned | Each hosted Base has a ceiling. As it approaches, Launchway says what is growing, offers cleanup and offers the guided move, and at the ceiling only the growing kind of data stops. |
| [Nothing held hostage](roadmap/milestone-7.md#nothing-held-hostage) | Planned | Every hosted Base can be exported completely, at any time, in an open and documented format with a verifier. |

### Never a place to park files

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Nothing anonymous or public](roadmap/milestone-7.md#nothing-anonymous-or-public) | Planned | No repository, artifact, image, page, report or file on the hosted service can be reached without signing in as a member of that Base. |
| [No general file storage](roadmap/milestone-7.md#no-general-file-storage) | Planned | The service holds repositories, build results and registry images that pipelines produce, and nothing else: there is no upload-a-file feature. |
| [Identity checks in proportion to risk](roadmap/milestone-7.md#identity-checks-in-proportion-to-risk) | Planned | A verified address, a second factor and limits that start low for a new account and rise as it shows normal use. |
| [Abuse reports, takedown and suspension](roadmap/milestone-7.md#abuse-reports-takedown-and-suspension) | Planned | A published way to report abuse, a process to act on it, suspension with an appeal, and detection that respects the promise that the operator cannot read your work. |
| [Customer files kept apart from the operator’s own systems](roadmap/milestone-7.md#customer-files-kept-apart-from-the-operator-s-own-systems) | Planned | Whatever outsiders store is kept on capacity separate from anything the operator runs for itself, with its own keys per Base. |

| [Stage 2: files on your own machines](roadmap/milestone-7.md#stage-2-files-on-your-own-machines) | Planned | The first public opening offers only the mode where files stay on your machines. Fully hosted is shown as coming, never as a choice that fails. |
| [Stage 3: fully hosted, on rented capacity](roadmap/milestone-7.md#stage-3-fully-hosted-on-rented-capacity) | Planned | Public sign-up with hosted storage, your own runners and takedown tools, on capacity rented for the purpose. |
| [Stage 4: hosted runners](roadmap/milestone-7.md#stage-4-hosted-runners) | Planned | Public sign-up with sandboxed runners run by the service. |

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|

A plan changes limits, never features, and a new account’s spend limit starts at zero, so nothing can be charged until its owner raises it. |

## Milestone 8: Zero-downtime delivery for anything, with Argo CD as a first-class citizen (Next)

Every deployment, whatever it is made of, brings the new version up beside the old one, proves it, moves traffic or work over in steps you can see and control, keeps watching afterward and returns to the last good state by itself if things get worse. [Detail page](roadmap/milestone-8.md).

### One model for every deployment

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Delivery plans](roadmap/milestone-8.md#delivery-plans) | Planned | Describe how a release rolls out as a plan kept in Git: the steps, how much at each, what to check and how careful to be. |
| [Shifters](roadmap/milestone-8.md#shifters) | Planned | The part of a plan that moves traffic or work to the new version: a traffic split, a load balancer pool, a queue reader or a function alias. |
| [Proofs](roadmap/milestone-8.md#proofs) | Planned | Checks that say whether a step is safe: metrics, test transactions, network health and database health, each with a verdict in a sentence. |
| [Guarded queries for monitoring data](roadmap/milestone-8.md#guarded-queries-for-monitoring-data) | In progress | Questions put to a metrics or log store pass through a guarded layer that limits what can be asked and how much comes back. |
| [The stable state](roadmap/milestone-8.md#the-stable-state) | Planned | For each environment Launchway records the version, settings, secret versions, toggles and routes that were known to work. |
| [Controls with consequences](roadmap/milestone-8.md#controls-with-consequences) | Planned | Go, go all the way, pause, resume, stop and go back, try again, skip a step, set the amount by hand, restart and scale. |
| [Safeguards on by default](roadmap/milestone-8.md#safeguards-on-by-default) | Planned | Every protection starts on and your team can tune or turn it off per project and environment; only a level above can require one. |
| [Rollout readiness scan](roadmap/milestone-8.md#rollout-readiness-scan) | Planned | Launchway reads your application and tells you what stands in the way of a safe rollout, with changes it proposes. |

### Rollouts: every strategy, with an assistant

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| [Every rollout strategy](roadmap/milestone-8.md#every-rollout-strategy) | Planned | Canary and blue-green, with all the step types, several analyses at once and experiments, created and shown in Launchway. |
| [An assistant for creating a rollout](roadmap/milestone-8.md#an-assistant-for-creating-a-rollout) | Planned | A few plain questions (what is it, how do users reach it, how do we know it is healthy, how careful, who must clear it) produce a plan, a picture and files in Git. |
| [The rollout panel](roadmap/milestone-8.md#the-rollout-panel) | In progress | One panel shows the line of steps, where traffic really goes next to where it is meant to go, every check as it measures, old and new side by side, and events in time order. |
| [Rehearsal environments](roadmap/milestone-8.md#rehearsal-environments) | Planned | Try a rollout in a short-lived environment with a traffic generator and injected faults before it reaches production. |
| [Return to any earlier version](roadmap/milestone-8.md#return-to-any-earlier-version) | Planned | Choose an earlier version and return to it, with what that will change spelled out first. |

### Guarded after the deploy, and back to stable by itself

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|

| [The watch](roadmap/milestone-8.md#the-watch) | Planned | After the last step, keep watching for a set time (30 minutes, for example) against a baseline of how the service normally behaves. |
| [Automatic return to stable](roadmap/milestone-8.md#automatic-return-to-stable) | Planned | If error rates or other signals worsen during the watch, Launchway returns to the last stable state and says why. |

|---|---|---|

## How we build

Throughout, not a milestone: the standard every item is held to.

- **Everything, without the mess.** Every feature uses the same objects, permissions, audit trail and policy point, and nothing switched off appears in the menus.
- **One way in, every way in.** A wizard for each task, with the same operation in the HTTP API, the agent endpoint, the command line and Terraform.
- **Only a database and Git.** Everything else is built in; outside integrations stay optional.
- **Boring upgrades.** One binary and a database, additive migrations, an older binary running on a newer schema, and rollback by image.
- **High availability and security are part of done.** A feature says what happens when a server, the database or a runner dies, and who may do what, before it merges.
- **Honest status.** An item is available only when it is merged, tested and documented. Order is by value and is not a schedule.
- **Security first.** Everything Launchway holds is encrypted at rest, every part runs with least privilege, and the secure choice is the default.
- **Help, never enforce or overwrite.** Launchway explains, proposes and previews. It never rewrites your application or infrastructure silently; you accept, edit or decline.
- **Safeguards on, the team in charge.** Every protection starts on and your team may tune or turn it off. Only a level above you, such as the Wing for production, can require one.
- **Never a button that does not work.** An action that cannot work here is absent or shown unavailable with the reason. A risky action that is allowed asks first, in plain words.
- **Everything optional, with built-in defaults.** Each capability has a built-in default and a popular backend you can use instead, so an installation needs the fewest tools.
- **The hosted service holds nothing sensitive.** Your network and your secrets stay with you, seen only through a small program that runs on your side.
- **Accessible to everyone.** Automated checks hold every screen, and the API, agent endpoint and command line, to a top-tier standard for keyboard, screen reader and contrast.
- **Simple to install, nothing assumed.** A handful of values, no secrets manager or identity provider required, and a guided first sign-in that is the same for everyone.
- **Every customer’s Base is walled off, and proven.** Isolation between customers is not a promise: tests try every route from one Base into another and gate every release.
- **A cache only makes a build faster.** It may never change a build’s result: what can change is looked up again, and a run says when it cannot be sure.
- **The system works out the order; a person can always override.** Build order, release order and branching patterns are worked out from your code, shown with their reasons, and open to correction.
